comment.narrative: No training programmes on European Studies for the Ukrainian politicians and civil servants
A special training program in European Studies established for Ukrainian politicians and civil servants with substantial financial resources allocated

To enhance capacity support for Ukrainian policymakers and civil servants on EU integration the Project team has developed a specialized training program in European Studies. This program is tailored for Ukrainian politicians and civil servants aiming to equip them with the necessary knowledge for Ukraines membership negotiations with the EU and its potential future participation in EU executive bodies. The team integrated two courses. European Integration 1 and European Integration 2 into the Masters in Public Policy and Governance MPPG program. These courses were designed to support the development of knowledge for the negotiation process. Courses were taught by KSE lecturer in Public Administration Nadiia Koval.To enhance capacity support Ukrainians current and future Ukrainian politicians and civil servants on EU integration the Project team continue work under improving of specialized training program in European Studies. This program current and future Ukrainian politicians and civil servants aiming to equip them with the necessary knowledge for Ukraines membership negotiations with the EU and its potential future participation in EU executive bodies.This program will allow graduates be able to formulate policies that meet EU standards and that will contribute to Ukraines further European integration. This program will be open to both current MPPG students and external participants.Currently the KSE project team is working on attracting new highly qualified lecturers who will add more quality and recognition to the courses as well as on the issue of recording courses on video and then posting them on publicly available platforms. During the next academic year we plan to offer this program to participants.

title.narrative: Number of capacity development initiatives funded under the Intervention that improve core Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) capacities

description.narrative: SDG 16 Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions.CSO core capacities relate, among others, to the following: Management expertise (organizational, administrative, financial management and resource mobilization) Technical expertise (related to thematic sectors of intervention) Lobby, advocacy, public policy making and watchdog roles Networking and coalition building CSO capacity development is aimed at increasing local CSOs capacity to perform their roles as independent development actors more effectively. Capacity development comprises the following characteristics: Actions aimed at overcoming capacity constraints ranging from limitations in technical management and leadership skills, fundraising, to results management and issues of internal governance. Support to the capacity development of CSOs will particularly include local actors, as part of a longterm, demanddriven and flexible approach, giving particular consideration to constituency building and representativeness. Capacity development will be based on local demand, include mentoring and coaching, peer learning, networking, and building of linkages from the local to the global level, also including longterm and equitable partnerships for capacity development between local and European CSOs. EU interventions that support CSOs to develop their core capacities can be considered for this indicator: Technical support (developing capacities through direct ad hoc, onthejob trainings or fostering transfer of knowhow from large, structured INGOs/CSOs to informal, emerging forms of civic engagement) Financial support (funding training, study visits or participation in capacity development initiatives).
